newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 25.

text.p: Itochu Corp and leading U.S. utility company Atlantic Richfield Co have bought three coal mines in the United States from Coastal Corp, a producer and trader of coal and natural gas. Itochu has paid about 2.4 billion yen of the total 70 billion yen price, which makes it the Japanese company with the biggest investment in a coal mine. The two companies plan to set up a management company in Novemver to sell coal in the United States as well as export coal to Japan and other parts of Asia.
Two Chinese companies are expected to list their shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in late 1997.

Japan Storage Battery Co Ltd is expected to increase its parent current profit for the business year ending March 31, 1997, by 17 percent from the previous year to about 3.6 billion yen. It is also expected to have increased its parent current profit for the half year to September 30 by 54 percent year-on-year to around 1.2 billion yen.

NTN Corp is expected to have doubled its operating profit for the half year ended September 30 from the previous-year level to more than 5.2 billion yen, helped by a decline in marketing costs and the yen's weakness.

Two leading telecommunications engineering companies are expected to expand their profits, helped by the growth in the mobile phone market. Nippon Comsys Corp is seen to have increased its parent current profit in the half year to September 30 by 48 percent from the previous year to 4.1 billion yen, while Kyowa Exeo Corp is seen to have increased its profit by 87 percent to three billion yen in the same period.

The nine companies in the DDI Pocket group plan to raise their combined capital by about 30 percent, or 7.65 billion yen, at the end of October by allocating new shares to Kyocera Corp. The move will raise Kyocera's stake in the personal handy phone (PHS) group from two to 24 percent. The group companies' balance sheets will be consolidated with Kyocera's after the capital increase. The total capital of the nine DDI companies is currently at 25.5 billion yen.

Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc plans to set up a subsidiary on April 1, 1997, to unify the operations of three resin operations in its business group. The new company, to be capitalised at 20 million yen, will handle product development, production and sales.
NEC Corp plans to set up a wholly owned company in China to provide system intergration services by the end of this year. The company hopes for annual sales of 10 billion yen by 2000.
